body.name: Transversal fixed-support fuzzy-hypothesis family
body.construction: Let \(\overline A_0=A_0\oplus I_{d-2}\), \(\overline A_1=A_1\oplus I_{d-2}\), and \(B_t=(1-t)\overline A_0+t\overline A_1\). The construction is admitted exactly for class constants for which there is \(\eta>0\) such that, whenever \(\lvert t-t_\star\rvert\le\eta\), the normalized quadratic potentials with Hessians \(\overline A_0\) and \(B_t\), their ellipsoidal supports, and their induced constant densities satisfy the restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_s\) with strict slack \(\eta\): Hessian eigenvalues lie in \([m+\eta,M-\eta]\), densities lie in \([b+\eta,B-\eta]\), the \(C^{s+2}\) potential and \(C^s\) density norms are at most \(L-\eta\), boundary-chart norms are at most \(L-\eta\), and principal curvatures lie in \([L^{-1}+\eta,L-\eta]\). Fix \(\kappa\in C_c^\infty(B(0,1))\) with \(\kappa(v)=\tfrac12v^{\mathsf T}(\overline A_1-\overline A_0)v\) for \(\lVert v\rVert_2\le1/3\). For sufficiently small \(h\), pack \(N\asymp h^{-d}\) disjoint balls \(U_j=u_j+hB(0,1)\) into one fixed interior subball of \(\Omega\), set \(\theta=ah^s\) and \(t_{-}=t_\star-\theta/2\), where \(a>0\) is fixed sufficiently small relative to \(\eta\). For the focal pair set \(\varphi_p(u)=\tfrac12u^{\mathsf T}\overline A_0u\), so \(H_p\equiv\overline A_0\), and set \(\varphi_q^+(u)=\tfrac12u^{\mathsf T}B_{t_{-}}u\), after subtracting their \(\Omega\)-means. Fix every non-focal regime to the same normalized \(\overline A_0\)-quadratic law. For component \(j\), change only regime \(q\) by setting \(\varphi_q^{(j)}(u)=\varphi_q^+(u)+\theta h^2\kappa((u-u_j)/h)\), again normalized. Use the common known supports \(D_p=\overline A_0\Omega\) and \(D_q=B_{t_{-}}\Omega\). Let \(f_q^+,f_q^{(j)}\) be the induced pushforward densities, \(e_j=f_q^{(j)}-f_q^+\), \(E_j=B_{t_{-}}U_j\), and let \(\mathbf P^+,\mathbf P_j,\mathbb P_n^+,\mathbb P_{j,n},\overline{\mathbb P}_{0,n}\) denote the corresponding SCMs, sample laws, and uniform null mixture. This collection is \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{LB}}\).
